Construction and Working of LVDT in Simple Steps

The construction and working of LVDT can be summed up in one line: one primary coil and two identical secondary coils are wound on a hollow former, and a movable soft iron core changes how much flux reaches each secondary, so the difference of the two secondary voltages tells the core position.

Step by Step Working

  1. An AC excitation voltage is applied to the central primary winding.
  2. The primary sets up an alternating magnetic flux through the soft iron core.
  3. The flux induces voltages Vs1 and Vs2 in the secondary windings S1 and S2.
  4. S1 and S2 are connected in series opposition, so output Vo = Vs1 minus Vs2.
  5. At the null position the core couples equally to both, so Vo is nearly zero.
  6. As the core moves, Vo rises in proportion to displacement, and its phase shows the direction.
Core positionVs1 vs Vs2Output voltagePhase with primary
At centre (null)EqualNearly zeroNot defined
Moved towards S1Vs1 greaterRises with displacementIn phase
Moved towards S2Vs2 greaterRises with displacement180 degrees out of phase

When you study an LVDT diagram and working, trace the flux path from the primary through the core to each secondary. A phase sensitive demodulator then converts the AC output into a DC signal whose sign gives direction and whose size gives displacement.
